task: cme-2016-2018 — CME Group Globex per-product-group holiday schedules for calendar years 2016, 2017 and 2018 (New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Presidents' Day, Good Friday, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving and the day after, Christmas, plus the observed-day and adjacent early-close days CME publishes on the same documents). Juneteenth is not applicable: CME Group published no Juneteenth schedule before 2022.
coverage: 36 dated entries covering 27 holiday observances and 9 adjacent days that CME publishes on the same holiday document (2016-11-25, 2016-12-23, 2017-07-03, 2017-11-24, 2017-12-22, 2018-07-03, 2018-11-23, 2018-12-24, 2018-12-26). 375 family rows, every one at tier T1 from CME Group's own published Globex holiday schedule for that holiday. Families recorded as CME prints them: Equity Index, Nikkei 225 (dollar), Interest Rates, FX, Energy, Metals, Grains and Oilseeds, Livestock, Dairy, Lumber, and Cryptocurrency once CME lists it. CME prints Energy and Metals on one row, whose printed label changes over the range ('Energy, Metals & DME Products' in 2016 and early 2017, 'Energy, Metals, Softs & DME Products' from the late-2017 sheets, and 'Energy, Metal, Softs & DME Products' -- singular 'Metal' -- on the 2018 MLK sheet), so the two families carry the same verbatim and each entry quotes the label its own document prints; the 2016 New Year's PDF likewise prints 'Interest Rate & FX Products' as one block. No 2016-2018 CME holiday document prints a Nikkei-specific line: the Nikkei 225 (dollar) contracts are inside the 'Equity Products' row/block, and each Nikkei entry says so. Cryptocurrency first appears as a printed row ('Bitcoin') in CME's revisions dated 'Dec 5, 2017' -- on the 2017 Christmas sheet and on the 2018 New Year's sheet -- and on every 2018 sheet thereafter; before CME's 17 December 2017 Bitcoin futures launch the family did not exist and is not recorded. SOURCES. 2016: the nine per-holiday Globex PDFs, taken from CME's own annual bundle cmegroup.com/tools-information/holiday-calendar/files/2016-holiday-calendars.zip (archived 2017-06-28), which carries the final revisions ('Last updated 1/4/2016', '2/16/2016', '5/19/2016', '5/24/2016', '10/27/2016', '11/8/2016'); plus the standalone 2016 New Year's PDF ('Last updated 12/16/2015', archived 2016-01-08). The earlier standalone captures of the 2016 PDFs ('Last updated 10/28/2015') are also saved and differ (wrong UTC offsets, a Monday grain open later withdrawn, livestock open times, and the Dec 23 agricultural early closes added); the later revision is served in every case. 2017 and 2018: CME published only the Excel per-product-group sheet for most holidays (a PDF exists only for 2017 New Year's), so each 2017/2018 entry is read from that sheet's own dated column headers ('Regular Fri. Close', 'Regular Close', 'Early Close', 'PCP', 'Pre-opening', 'Open', 'Halt', 'Close'). For 2017 and 2018 the same annual-bundle channel used for 2016 is now used throughout: 2017-holiday-calendars.zip (archived 2021-01-26) and 2018-holiday-calendars.zip (archived 2026-08-30) carry CME's final revisions and supersede eight of the per-file captures (2017 Thanksgiving and Christmas; 2018 Good Friday, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas). Where a bundle copy is byte-identical to the per-file capture (2018 MLK, 2018 Presidents' Day, 2018 New Year's) the per-file citation is kept. Where the archive holds two digests for the same sheet URL, the later capture is served and the earlier is saved beside it. ZONE. Every 2017/2018 verbatim ends '[sheet: All times are Central Time, ET +1]', which is a bracketed annotation of the sheet's own printed zone rule, not part of the quoted cell text; every cited 2017/2018 sheet was checked and all print 'All times are Central Time  ET +1'. The printed UTC offset on the same line is NOT constant and is therefore not carried: it is +6 on the winter sheets and +5 on the summer ones, and CME's own 2017 Labor Day sheet changed from +6 to +5 between revisions. The ET value in close_instant/open_instant is CT+1 by the sheet's own rule; the 2016 PDFs print CT, ET and UTC themselves and are quoted as printed, including CME's own defects (the 2016 MLK PDF's '17100 ET' typo, and the 2016 Memorial Day PDF's Monday line, which prints '0000' with no UTC label). The 2016 PDFs use an en dash in lines such as '1600 CT / 1700 ET / 2200 UTC - Regular close'; every verbatim in this file normalises that single character to an ASCII hyphen, uniformly and throughout; it likewise collapses runs of whitespace inside a quoted row label, drops a label's trailing parenthetical cross-reference (the Christmas sheets print 'Energy, Metals, Softs & DME  products   (see notes below)'), and drops the '**' footnote marker from column headers such as 'Pre-opening**'. RETRIEVAL. cmegroup.com returns 403 to this machine, so every artifact is the Internet Archive's raw `id_` replay of the original cmegroup.com URL. All bytes, an INDEX.md with each document's URL, capture time in UTC and sha256, and the CDX enumeration that found them are in /Users/agedvagabond/Developer/exchange-hours-research/holidays/raw/cme-2016-2018 and, for the round-2 additions, in /Users/agedvagabond/Developer/exchange-hours-research/holidays/raw/cme-2016-2018-fix . Retrieved 2026-09-12 (UTC). A 'document' value is the file name under https://www.cmegroup.com/tools-information/holiday-calendar/files/ followed by '@' and the UTC date of the Internet Archive capture that was read; a value of the form '<year>-holiday-calendars.zip#<file> @<date>' names the file inside CME's annual bundle captured on that date. Files named '...--<yyyymmdd>' in the store are the later of two differing captures of the same URL. ROUND 2 (2026-09-12 UTC). The round-1 result is kept verbatim at /Users/agedvagabond/Developer/exchange-hours-research/holidays/cme-2016-2018.r1.json. It failed on source selection: it used CME's annual bundle for 2016 and never tried the 2017 or 2018 bundles, both of which are archived and both of which carry later CME revisions. Both bundles were retrieved, independently re-fetched and byte-compared, and every family row on every affected date was re-derived from their bytes. Changes: 2017-12-25 Cryptocurrency was 'unknown' with a 'missing' entry claiming the channels were exhausted -- the final revision prints a Bitcoin row, so the row is now sourced ('closed') and that 'missing' entry is deleted; the same revision prints a Bitcoin row for 2017-12-22, which is added; 2017-12-25 Grains and Oilseeds loses the Monday-evening 19:00 leg that CME withdrew in the same 'Dec 5, 2017' edit it made to the 2018 New Year's sheet, and its Tuesday pre-open moves 08:00 -> 06:00; 2018-07-03 Cryptocurrency moves from 'normal' (Regular Close 16:00) to 'early_close' (Early Close 12:15); 2018-12-25 Cryptocurrency's blank-cell caveat is deleted because the final revision fills the 'Globex Closed' cell in; a new 2018-12-26 entry records the Equity-only Wednesday 15:15/15:30 phase that only the final revision prints; 140 rows on 13 dates are re-keyed to the bundle documents; the disputed 2018-01-01 grain leg is resolved by reading the two intermediate revisions the round-1 task never fetched, which dates CME's withdrawal exactly; and two transcription slips are corrected against the PDF bytes (a 'UTC' token the 2016 Memorial Day PDF does not print, and 'Tuesday. Jan 19' on the 2016 MLK PDF). The evidence store was also corrected: the two 2016 New Year's documents the 2016-01-01 rows actually read are now listed in raw/cme-2016-2018/INDEX.md with URL, capture time and sha256, dl4_list.txt is listed under Enumeration, and raw/cme-2016-2018/cdx_trading_hours.json -- which was in fact the Internet Archive's 503 'Temporarily Offline' HTML page saved under a .json name -- is renamed cdx_trading_hours.FAILED.html and annotated as a failed fetch.
